data.hypothesis: Staging each source tile's x, y, z, and mass once in shared memory lets the active target threads in a block reuse those values, potentially reducing repeated global source loads. The interaction order and arithmetic are retained; synchronization and staging overhead may offset any benefit, so the official geometric-mean timing must decide.
data.notes: Dynamic shared memory is sized for four floats per 256-thread block. Tail lanes load only valid sources but reach every barrier; partial tiles use their valid count, and the source loop remains ordered. No fresh candidate correctness or timing result is available; the controller should evaluate it.
transformations: Stage source x, y, z, and mass into four dynamic shared-memory arrays, one source per lane per tile.
Process tiles in ascending source-index order, with unconditional block barriers around tile consumption and valid-count handling for partial tiles.
Set dynamic shared memory to 4096 bytes for the configured 256-thread block; preserve the baseline force and integration arithmetic.
